title: Machiko Hasegawa's birth chart
metaDescription: Machiko Hasegawa's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 8.9° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Venus holds a sextile to Uranus at 0.4° — close enough to weld taste to disruption. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 8.9° into Aquarius — the first decan, which the old scheme hands to Saturn. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 4.2° Aquarius, Venus at 0.8° Capricorn, Mars at 29.3° Libra. Mercury in an air sign reads as thought that travels by comparison; Venus in an earth sign reads as attraction that grows by reliability; Mars in an air sign reads as effort aimed through strategy and words.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Venus and Uranus hold the closest angle here — a sextile, 0.4° wide. A sixth of the circle is close enough for cooperation and far enough that it stays optional. Behind it, Mars trine Uranus at 1.1°, and the Sun opposition Neptune at 1.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks two placements here. The Sun in Aquarius at 8.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Libra at 29.3° is in detriment. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 3 air, 2 earth, 2 fire, 2 water by element and 4 fixed, 3 cardinal, 2 mutable by mode. Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Taurus into Gemini during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.2° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
